analysis:
Examined the per-request stopStringScope plumbing. EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift adds an optional stopStringScope parameter at head lines 63, 83 and 136-138. It is forced to nil for CBv2NativeBlockEngine at head lines 325-329. Head line 1073 passes cbv2Request.stopStringScope to runPump instead of the bridge-level scope. EngineV2Bridge.swift lines 124-125 change only a doc comment. The remaining submission body at head lines 526-1089 was reviewed as surrounding context: shared-KV reservation, prefix staging and abandon paths, deadline checks, retirement transfer and the pump handoff. Those resource-release paths, including the T-041 staging backstops, show no visible change in this PR.

Stop-string scope affects only where client stop strings match generated output: the reasoning region versus the whole text. It touches no encryption (T-008), cache salt or SSD naming (T-041), attestation (TB-009/TB-011) or billing paths. Choosing which stop string or region applies is a consumer-controlled output-shaping choice, not a trust escalation.

The pump receiving the request scope keeps the matched and reported stop consistent. For native block engines, the nil override makes the bridge's matching agree with the decoder's whole-output matching.

The source of the per-request scope is not visible here; it may come from a ReasoningStopScope derived from request fields. Integration should confirm it is derived from validated request fields and cannot make the pump suppress or truncate output in a way that misreports completion tokens for usage/billing. Usage counting appears to be engine-sourced, so this is unlikely to be material.

No security regression was identified.
